jarvlabs.name: JarvLabs
jarvlabs.shortDesc: Independent digital studio building in-house products from Colombia for LATAM.
longDesc: Studio's root site — the home where the products live (Citook, Pagetook) and where the conversation with potential clients happens. Designed as a statement: a few products, well crafted, with taste.

Mobile-first editorial layout, no services catalog, no premature pricing. The journey takes the reader from the promise (curated digital products) to the proof (each product solves a concrete problem) and from there to the manifesto and contact.

Tech decisions: Next.js 16 with App Router, Tailwind v4 with OKLCH tokens, motion/react for editorial reveals, light/dark locked to light for now. Zero cheap gradients; visual weight is carried by typography and a lime accent used sparingly.
highlights: Custom typography system (Fraunces display + Satoshi body) self-hosted with next/font.
OKLCH tokens — electric lime accent stable in color mixes (color-mix in oklch).
One-page with scroll-spy + URL hash cleanup for SEO and clean deep links.
Performance: Lighthouse 96+, no heavy UI libraries, CSS-only mockups.

pagetook.name: Pagetook
pagetook.shortDesc: Agency brand to build websites with AI in days — not months — for entrepreneurs and businesses across LATAM.
longDesc: Consumer brand of the studio focused on closing the gap between 'I want a website' and 'it's live'. Aggressive positioning against the traditional agency: days, not months, and no inflated pricing.

Deep multipage structure: home with a strong value-prop, services page, real-cases portfolio, transparent pricing plans, manifesto, and a quote form. Each section is built with editorial motion and CSS micro-mockups showing 'before vs after' working with the brand.

Main challenge: communicate speed without sounding cheap. Solved with direct copy, real production cases, and a visual system that feels premium (detailed mockups, oversized typography, smooth animations) without falling into agency clichés.
highlights: 'Traditional agency vs Pagetook' comparison with animated CSS mockups.
Portfolio section with preview cards per delivered project.
FAQ accordion with honest copy about process, price, and timing.
Quote form with automatic project-type classification.

citook.name: Citook
citook.role: Design + development of the marketing site
citook.shortDesc: B2B SaaS product: the WhatsApp conversation that fills the agenda for clinics, salons, and beauty centers.
longDesc: Marketing site for the studio's SaaS product. Sells a behavior change (no more chasing clients by phone) using a 'before/after' narrative built on top of real WhatsApp and admin panel mockups.

Each section has a specific mockup that shows the benefit concretely: the conversation that confirms a booking, the morning dashboard panel, automatic cancellation recovery, the weekly report that lands in the owner's inbox.

Challenge: show value without a live demo. Solved with animated WhatsApp mockups (each message appearing sequentially with realistic timing) and a dashboard skeleton with believable data. The user 'sees how it works' without having to request access.
highlights: Animated WhatsApp conversation mockup (sequential messages with typing indicators).
CSS-only dashboard skeleton with daily metrics and agenda.
Weekly Gantt-style view showing cancellation recovery.
Mock weekly report that simulates the real email the client receives.

toolstacksuite.name: ToolStackSuite
toolstacksuite.shortDesc: Free utility suite for devs and creators: QR generator, passwords, JSON, UUID, Base64, JWT, hashes, UTM builder. No sign-up, all in the browser.
longDesc: SaaS platform of utilities — the kind of tools a dev uses once a month and ends up on any sketchy site full of ads. The proposal is the opposite: a single clean suite, bilingual, no tracking, no login, no usage caps.

Current catalog: customizable QR generator, password generator with fine-grained control, JSON formatter/minifier/validator, UUID v4 generator, Base64 encoder, URL encoder, JWT decoder with header + payload visualization, hash generator (SHA-1/256/384/512), and a UTM link builder for campaigns. Each tool is its own page with supporting copy (inline FAQ, use cases, exporting).

Key tech decision: everything is processed in the browser (zero-trust backend). Tools that touch sensitive data — passwords, JWT, hashes, JSON — never send the input to a server. That's a feature, not a detail: the user knows their data never leaves the tab.
highlights: 9+ online tools, all client-side (zero data sent to the server).
Bilingual from day one (ES/EN) with instant switching.
Technical SEO: each tool with its own route, meta tags, and FAQ schema.org.
Zero ads, zero registration, zero input tracking — privacy as a feature.

orinoco.name: Orinoco Sanduchería
orinoco.shortDesc: Artisan sandwich shop in Yopal with bread baked daily. Editorial one-page with photo menu, story, and WhatsApp ordering.
longDesc: Client case delivered under the Pagetook brand. An artisan sandwich shop in Yopal that needed a serious digital presence but didn't want an app: WhatsApp orders, the story behind the brand, and a menu with a hero product in every slot.

Design decisions: display typography with personality (Fraunces for the headlines), warm palette reflecting the product flavor, generous photography of the bread and sandwiches, scroll micro-animations that add rhythm without distracting.
The site started generating WhatsApp orders from the first week online — conversion happens directly in the chat, with no intermediate form. Zero friction.
highlights: Editorial one-page with menu, process story, and location.
Interactive map of the venue with a direct Google Maps route.
Primary CTA deep-links to WhatsApp with a prefilled message.
Hero with full-bleed product photography and typographic lockup.

caribevan.name: CaribeVan
caribevan.shortDesc: Private van with driver for family trips to the Colombian Caribbean. Direct WhatsApp booking, no forms.
longDesc: Client case delivered under the Pagetook brand. A family-run tourist transport operation in the Colombian Caribbean that needed to convey trust (safe van, driver who knows the region) in under 30 seconds.

One-page structure with three clear blocks: destinations (with real geographic coordinates as an editorial detail), postcards from past trips (testimonials styled as travel tickets), and vehicle specs (formatted as a 'route sheet' with small numbers and technical typography).

Challenge: balance the Caribbean imagery (color, warmth, joy) with the seriousness of a family travel decision. Solved with a deep-blue + solar-yellow accent palette, documentary photography, and editorial micro-details (cards signed by the driver, airline-style route numbers).
highlights: Destinations section with geographic coordinates as an editorial detail.
Postcard-testimonials styled as signed travel tickets.
Vehicle route sheet with airline-style numbered specs.
Single CTA: WhatsApp booking, no form.

daniel-demo-reel.name: Daniel G. · Demo Reel
daniel-demo-reel.shortDesc: Demo reel and portfolio for Daniel Galindo, a 2D animator specialized in Toon Boom Harmony. Editorial one-page with embedded video reel, projects, and bio.
longDesc: Portfolio case for a 2D animator. The challenge: the site had to feel as carefully crafted as the work it shows — a demo reel is the first professional impression; it couldn't fight the video for the spotlight, but it couldn't disappear either.

One-page layout with clear narrative hierarchy: hero with embedded video reel + editorial 'spec sheet' (duration, resolution, framerate), individual project section, bio, and contact. The heavy-stroke display typography gives identity without competing with the reel's color.

Tech details: EN/ES + light/dark toggle on the client side, video embedded via Vimeo (better than YouTube for showreels because of privacy and branding), scroll micro-animations adding rhythm between sections. Deployed on Vercel — fast and frictionless to iterate copy based on client feedback.
highlights: Hero with embedded video reel and editorial spec sheet (duration, resolution, fps).
Bilingual ES/EN + light/dark toggle with persistent preferences.
Individual projects section with thumbnails and role context.
Display typography with personality — identity without stealing the reel's spotlight.

koaladevs.name: KoalaDevs
koaladevs.shortDesc: Design and web development studio in Bogotá. Corporate site with services, process, plans, and FAQ.
longDesc: Previous iteration — the site where I learned what later became the foundation of the current studio. Classic corporate structure (services, process, benefits, plans, FAQ) but already with the brand-mascot pattern and a consistent palette.

I keep it in the portfolio because it's the honest version of the journey: not everything I build is Next.js 16 with OKLCH tokens. KoalaDevs was where many decisions were first tested (editorial plans section, FAQ accordion, integrated contact form) that were later refined in Pagetook.
Lighter stack (HTML + Tailwind, deployed on Cloudflare Pages) — fit-for-purpose for a services landing without login or dashboard. Site speed is still excellent.
highlights: Plans system with comparable cards and a CTA per tier.
4-step workflow with contextual micro-explanations.
Accessible accordion FAQ with direct copy.
Consistent brand mascot across the experience.
